title: From Hobby to Passion: Tanzanian UI/UX Designer Overcomes Challenges to Pursue Passion
summary: A personal account of developing a UI/UX design career in Tanzania through curiosity, collaboration and perseverance.

content.text: I am Joseph Masonda, a freelance UI/UX designer from Morogoro, Tanzania. I have been in the design industry for three years, and I am excited to share my journey.

My journey began as a hobby that quickly became a passion. I fell in love with UI/UX design and knew I wanted it to become my primary source of income. Along the way, I faced challenges, including a small design community in Tanzania and limited project opportunities for growth.

Despite these challenges, I remained determined. Collaborating with others in the industry became an important way to grow my skills and learn new techniques. I also joined design communities to interact with fellow designers and receive feedback on my work.

One of my notable achievements was working on Ujuzi Connect, an online placement system for university students, graduates and professionals seeking opportunities as volunteers, interns and field practitioners. The project allowed me to showcase my skills and work with other professionals.

Through the journey, I learned that teaching others and sharing work with peers for feedback are essential for self-growth. I also came to value curiosity as the key to learning every day from anyone and any source.

As a Tanzanian UI/UX designer, I hope to inspire other designers to pursue their passions despite the challenges they may face. The design industry in Tanzania is growing, and I am excited to be part of it. My advice to anyone beginning in the field is simple: keep pushing, keep learning and keep growing.

My journey as a UI/UX designer in Tanzania is a reminder of the power of perseverance, collaboration and self-growth. Despite the challenges, I have stayed passionate about my work and continued to develop my skills through learning and collaboration.
